capabilities: Send HTTP requests with methods, params, headers, auth and file or structured bodies
Inspect responses as pretty-printed JSON, HTML previews, images or PDFs with timing breakdowns
Import collections and environments from Postman, Insomnia, Bruno, HTTPie, Hoppscotch, curl, HAR and .http files
Manage collections, folders and environments as OpenCollection YAML files with shared variables and auth
Keep a local-only history of sent requests with their responses
extras: Desktop only and requires Obsidian 1.11.4 or later; no account, cloud or telemetry. The 'Coming next' section lists unimplemented features such as GraphQL, gRPC, scripts, a collection runner and mobile support.
problem: Testing APIs normally means switching to an external tool like Postman, while Obsidian has no built-in HTTP client and API collections live outside the vault.

relations.evidence: Import from Postman, Insomnia, Bruno, HTTPie, Hoppscotch, curl, HAR and .http files, environments included.
Collections are plain YAML files in the OpenCollection format that Bruno uses.
Import from Postman, Insomnia, Bruno, HTTPie, Hoppscotch, curl, HAR and .http files, environments included.

summary: REST API testing client that sends HTTP requests, inspects JSON responses, and stores collections as plain YAML files in the vault.
